name: Student visa (Study in Saudi Arabia programme)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires admission to a recognised Saudi university or institution, sponsoring the student's visa via the Ministry of Education's international-student channels.
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission from a Saudi institution participating in the 'Study in Saudi Arabia' programme.

requirements.blocker_text: The institution acts as the sponsor for the student's residence permit (Iqama); a self-sponsored student route also exists for a narrower set of applicants who can demonstrate independent financial means.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the institution will sponsor the visa, or qualify for the self-sponsored track if not institution-sponsored.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires proof of sufficient financial means (personal funds, family sponsorship, or a scholarship) for tuition and living costs, plus mandatory health insurance.
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements, a scholarship award letter, or a sponsor's financial guarantee.

evidence_required.document: Admission letter from a Saudi institution
Proof of funds or scholarship award

outcome.duration_length: tied to programme length, renewed annually via the Iqama

sources.title: Ministry of Education -- Study in Saudi Arabia programme (official)

notes: HONEST SOURCING GAP, flagged rather than guessed around: unlike Poland's student route, foreign students in Saudi Arabia generally have NO work rights on a standard student Iqama -- this is the opposite of Poland's uncapped student work rights and worth surfacing prominently on any cross-country comparison view. A narrower part-time work allowance exists in practice for some scholarship categories and postgraduate researchers, but the exact scope and any hour caps were not conclusively confirmed against a primary Ministry of Education or HRSD source in this research pass; work_rights is set to 'none' as the safe, verified default for the standard case rather than asserting a partial allowance that couldn't be pinned down. status is published rather than draft because the core admission/sponsorship/funds requirements are solidly tier-1 sourced; the narrower work-rights question is the specific gap, not the route's core eligibility test.
